requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the cluster's internal time source.
requirements.summary: Node1 persistently serves NTP on 10.100.154.10:123, permits the internal subnet, and is synchronized. After a bounded reboot it returned with a different boot ID, the same configuration, a running listener, and healthy synchronization; node2 subsequently selected it as its peer.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize only against node1 rather than a public time server.
requirements.summary: Node2's final configuration contains only server 10.100.154.10, and direct status shows that peer selected with sync_ntp, stratum 4, and refid 10.100.154.10. The same configuration and synchronized state recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed legacy operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes began on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic and installed ntpd 4.2.4. Final and post-reboot observations retain that kernel, and the legacy ntpd implementation is directly shown running and synchronizing successfully on both nodes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered configuration/service/synchronization, and an after-executor boot identity matching the final post-restart observation.
limitations: The lifecycle collector could not assess failed services through systemd because this legacy platform does not provide systemctl; direct SysV/process checks nevertheless show the relevant NTP services healthy.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory backup files under /etc, so their final presence is inferred from explicit creation and the absence of any later removal command.
The after-executor platform probe reports the retained kernel but not the Ubuntu release label; Ubuntu 7.10 is directly observed initially, and the trace contains no operating-system upgrade action.

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional configuration and final restart protocol were well controlled, package health remained clean, and /tmp had no final residue. Most intermediate restarts and corrections had a clear diagnostic role: they exposed the ntpdate conflict and legacy boot-order races. Hygiene is reduced by retained package-init modifications on both nodes from cmd-ba5efa1898c746f1 and cmd-d37e4a96f39c4d47; these proved insufficient on the subsequent node2 reboot and were superseded by the working if-up hooks, but were not reverted. Several rollback copies also remained with no demonstrated final operational role: ntp.conf.pre-internal-time from cmd-584a5a1e819347a8 and cmd-0dae577a4ecf4d81, ntpdate.pre-internal-time from cmd-6109312bb7314fa1 and cmd-fe612e496bbd4fc9, and ntp.pre-ipv4-wait from cmd-ba5efa1898c746f1 and cmd-d37e4a96f39c4d47. These were retained rather than cleaned up.
